name: Other Immunodeficiency Syndromes Due to Defects in Innate Immunity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Immunological Diagnostic Criteria for Innate Immunodeficiency Syndromes

criteria.description: Recurrent, severe, or unusual infections suggestive of innate immune dysfunction
Abnormal results in innate immune function assays (e.g., neutrophil oxidative burst, complement activity)
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting innate immunity
Exclusion of secondary immunodeficiencies and other primary immunodeficiencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent severe infections plus abnormal innate immune function assays with exclusion of secondary causes; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is increasingly important for precise diagnosis and subclassification.

pathognomonic.notes: Detected by dihydrorhodamine (DHR) test or nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) test
Indicative of innate immune defects affecting fungal defense

common.notes: Persistent fungal infections of skin and mucosa
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

common.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic infection or immune activation
Poor growth secondary to recurrent infections
searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

common.notes: Raised CRP and ESR during infectious episodes

occasional.notes: Autoimmune cytopenias or other autoimmune phenomena
Non-caseating granulomas due to dysregulated inflammation
searchTerms: clumps of immune cells in tissues

occasional.notes: Due to infections or inflammatory bowel involvement

rare.symptomName: Severe anaphylactic reactions to blood products
rare.notes: Due to anti-IgA antibodies in some patients
Chronic lung damage from recurrent infections

laboratory: Abnormal neutrophil oxidative burst test (DHR or NBT)
Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) during infections
Lymphopenia or neutropenia in some cases
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing recurrent pneumonia or lung abscesses
MRI brain in cases with neurological complications
Ultrasound or CT for lymphadenopathy or granulomas
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as NCF1, CYBB, MYD88, IRAK4, or others affecting innate immunity
Variants identified by targeted gene panels or whole exome sequencing
other: Positive family history in some cases
Poor response to standard antimicrobial therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Specific defect in NADPH oxidase complex
Profound T and B cell deficiency
Absent or very low lymphocyte counts

redFlags: Recurrent life-threatening bacterial or fungal infections
Poor or absent response to standard antimicrobial treatments
Family history of early infant deaths or immunodeficiency
references: Picard C, et al. Primary Immunodeficiencies Associated with Defects in Innate Immunity. Immunol Rev. 2015.
Orange JS, et al. The Diagnosis and Management of Primary Immunodeficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.
Orphanet Report Series: Primary Immunodeficiencies. Orphanet. 2023.
